To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The trans-13-octadeconic acid isomer (trans-13t-octadecenoyl) is a highly selective inhibitor of the incorporation of fatty acids into human plasma lipoproteins.

trans- and cis-isomers of 13-octadece-enoic acid (18:1Δ13) are selectively excluded from incorporation into plasma lipids, and the cis- and trans- isomers are incorporated differently into plasma lipids.

the cis 13- and 9-18:1 fatty acids are not equally distributed among the human plasma lipid classes and that the trans 13-18 fatty acid isomer is not preferentially distributed in the human plasma lipid fraction that is preferentially distributed to adipose tissue.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the incorporation of deuterium labeled trans and cis 18:1 isomeric fatty acids in the human plasma lipid fractions.
the absorption, transport, and distribution of the 13-octadeconoic acid isomers in human plasma lipoproteins.
the incorporation of the two geometric isomers of 13-octade-cenoic acid into the human plasma lipids and the distribution of these two isomers into plasma lipoprotein classes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
trans fatty acids are not incorporated into human plasma lipids in the same way as cis fatty acids.
the human plasma lipid system selectively excludes the 13t and 13c isomers from incorporation into all lipid classes.
the trans-13-octadeconoic acid isomer is not a good candidate as a dietary fatty acid for lowering plasma cholesterol levels in man.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 13t and 13c isomers of 18:1 are not equally distributed in plasma lipids, with the 13t isomer being excluded from the phospholipid and cholesteryl esters.
the human body is capable of absorbing the 13t and 13c isomers of octadecenoic but that they are not well distributed to the plasma lipids.
the human plasma lipids selectively discriminate against the trans isomers relative to the cis isomers of 13-18 and 9-18 fatty acids.
The main takeaway from our work is that
13t- and 13c-octadecadienoic acid is not well incorporated into human plasma lipids, and the cis isomer was more poorly incorporated than the trans isomer.
the trans isomer is excluded in all lipoprotein classes, whereas the cis isomer is excluded from cholesteryl esters and 2- and 3-acyl phospholipids.
the 13t isomer is excluded from incorporation into human plasma lipids and is selectively incorporated into the 1-acylglycerophospholipid fraction.
